verdict.rationale: Hightouch's own Identity Resolution writes unified identities and a one-row-per-identity Golden Record table into the warehouse, which data engineers can query directly. Hightouch Events lands event history in the same warehouse, and Customer Studio builds traits on top, so a documented profile store exists. However, the docs say Hightouch does not store or serve profiles itself, and its REST API covers only syncs, models, sources and destinations, so there is no profile lookup API. missing for 10: a documented profile/trait lookup API, explicit documentation of a unified profile schema joining traits, identifiers and event history, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a data engineer, I can query unified customer profiles — traits, identifiers, event history — through a documented profile API or store

citations.quote: Golden Record — a one-row-per-identity table of canonical field values (selected by survivorship rules) that many teams use as their source-of-truth customer or account view.
Query these directly, build models on them in Customer Studio, or sync them downstream.
Identity Resolution unifies a person's identifiers into one resolved identity, and Customer Studio builds traits and audiences on top.
Hightouch Events collects customer behavior from websites, mobile apps, and backend systems, then stores that data in your warehouse.
